Bring your favorite materials, settle in, listen to some good tunes in great company, and get into your flow. This will be a great opportunity to create a more finished work of art, hone your portraiture skills, or work with a material that you don’t normally get to use. Our model will be dressed in character (more details coming soon) and serve as our muse for the afternoon. Whether you want to loosen up your line work, push into a sustained study, or simply spend a slow Sunday afternoon drawing from life, this is your space to do it. item.title: The Assembly of Lovers - Sufi Drum Circle — Mon Aug 31, 7:00 PM — the Space
item.description: Community drum and chant circle rooted in Sufi prayer. Meets every other Monday: August 31, September 14, September 28, etc. Contribution: Sliding scale donation $20–$40 (no one will be turned away) This is a vibrant Community Drum and Chanting Circle, where we drum and chant from our hearts into the universe. This experience is open to absolutely everyone, regardless of background or belief system—all that’s required is an open heart and a willingness to connect through sound. The term ‘lover’ in this context refers to seekers on the Sufi path who are longing for union with the divine energy. You can think of this gathering as an expansion of the sema sufi meditations we used to offer. It is looser in form, more focused on music, and does not necessarily involve whirling, although it is welcome if you are called to it. There is a rhythm older than thought. item.title: Tuesday Night Figure Drawing - Open Studio — Tue Sep 1, 7:00 PM — the Space
item.description:
Tuesday Night Figure Drawing – Open Studio *Cover art by Ling Chen.
Tuesday night at The Space is your invitation to drop in, find your creative flow, and feel good. Each week a different nude model serves as our muse as we pursue creative expression through observation and mark making. We challenge how we see and what we want to say — observing the nuances of the human form, its moods, character, and light — and do our best to capture something in the moment that tells a story. This has become a tight-knit, supportive community of seekers — artists, experimenters, and curious souls drawn together by the shared pursuit of capturing the living human form. Use the time to refine your skills, experiment with different media, and deepen your understanding of anatomy, gesture, and proportion. item.title: Mindful Masculinity Men’s Group — Wed Sep 2, 7:00 PM — The Space
item.description:
We Meet Bi-Weekly Every Other Wednesday | 7 – 8:30 pm | $15
Through open dialogue, mindfulness, and other calming practices we quiet the mind, open the heart, and deepen our connection to ourselves and each other. The meetings are hosted by Leo, mindfulness coach, teacher, and dad. We start by sharing our wins and challenges, honoring each voice without judgment or advice. We dive into practices that help us release stress, shift perspectives, and bring awareness and resilience into our lives. Each week, we focus on a different topic to help guide our lives. Together, we explore themes of trust, accomplishments, family, rest, intimacy, and presence — discovering new ways to move through the world as mindful men. Come as you are. Leave more grounded, connected, and inspired. Connect with Leo: Instagram @holdingpresence Online: HoldingPresence.com E-Mail: pe***********@***il.com

item.title: Apricot Sky Productions Presents 'Tributes: A Night of One-Acts and Monologues' — Sat Sep 12, 8:00 AM — Grove Street Theatre
item.description: Apricot Sky Productions presents “Tributes,” two nights of new one-act plays and monologues by New Jerseyans, benefiting the National September 11 Memorial & Museum Twenty-five years after the attacks that reshaped this state, Apricot Sky Productions will stage Tributes, an evening of six short plays and three monologues, on Friday, September 11 and Saturday, September 12 at 8 p.m. at the Grove Street Theater. Admission is free. A $20 donation is suggested at the door, with all proceeds going to the National September 11 Memorial & Museum in New York City. The work is written by Livingston playwright Eric Alter and performed and directed entirely by New Jersey artists, many of whom watched that morning unfold from their own front steps. New Jersey lost roughly 700 residents on September 11, 2001. “I will never forget the loss of humanity we experienced firsthand,” Alter said. “We aren’t helpless. item.description:
Monthly Gathering | Thursday, September 17th | 7:00 PM – 8:30 PM | The Space | $25 Calling all tarot lovers, both new and seasoned! Join us for an intimate way of exploring the cards. What could be better than a cozy evening of warm tea and deep conversation? Join us for Tea & Tarot with Gina Devine—a monthly, book club-style discussion group created to deepen our connection with the archetypes of the tarot through community and shared insight. Rather than a formal class, this is a casual meet-up where we treat the tarot as a living text. Saturday September 19 | 1 – 3 pm, $40 Breathe. Move. Create. Facilitated by Niraj Shah – long-time qi-gong teacher and practitioner, and Naz Botas – artist and owner of the Space. If you’ve been craving a gentle reset—something grounding, nourishing, and expressive—this workshop is your invitation. In this two-hour workshop, you’ll move through repeating cycles of Qi Gong and intuitive art-making designed to calm your nervous system, soften tension in the body, and open your creative heart. You’ll experience:
Qi Gong: slow, mindful movements paired with gentle breathwork to flow your energy and bring you into the present moment Intuitive Art: using charcoal, ink, or pastels, you’ll make marks on wall-length paper as your body moves — both naturally and through guided Qi Gong sequences — allowing your inner experience to express itself visually

item.description: Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More! Join us for this very interesting point to point hike in our Schuylkill River series! Distance will be about 15 miles and feature the Schuylkill River Trail, but also a lot of very interesting other things.... After meeting at the Schuylkill River Trail/Bartrum Trailhead on Market Street next to the Dry Wall place in Auburn PA, we will shuttle with as few vehicles as possible to the beginning. The hike will begin covering the trail system at Kaercher Creek Park, which we've never visited before. We'll weave around on most of their entire trail system, and then make our way through ball fields, and into downtown Hamburg. We'll get on the Schuylkill River Trail here and mostly follow it back to Auburn area, but with some surprise side trips along the way.
